This winter · The finish line is in sight

Four needs stand between steel and sanctuary

Work this winter depends on four immediate needs. Fund one outright, lead with a major gift, or give any amount toward the one that moves you — every dollar is a stud in the wall, an inch of glass, a foot of pipe.

I.

Framing

$220,000

Light-gauge metal framing forms the interior walls of the chapel and its adjoining spaces. Finishing it means the chapel rooms take their final shape — you will be able to stand where the sacristy, the nave, and the side chapels will be.

Share of winter goal7.1%
II.

Glass & Glazing

$1,408,000

A chapel is a house of light. The tall windows of the chapel and sacristy — and the doors and windows throughout — will close the building against the New England winter and let the light in. This is the largest single need, and the one that transforms the shell into a sanctuary.

Share of winter goal45.3%
III.

Concrete

$232,000

The remaining concrete work — the floors and slabs on which everything else stands. Unseen when it is done, and the reason everything above it can last for generations.

Share of winter goal7.5%
IV.

Plumbing, Electrical & HVAC

$1,250,000

Water, light, and heat: the systems that will let Mass, the Liturgy of the Hours, and silent prayer be celebrated in the chapel in every season — through a Boston January as faithfully as a June morning.

Share of winter goal40.2%

This winter · Nov 2026 — Giving Tuesday, Dec 1
Happening now

Walls, light, floors, and warmth

Framing, glass and glazing, concrete, and the building systems — the $3,110,000 winter push that closes the building in and gives the chapel its final shape.

Next

Stone, finishes, and the altar

Exterior stone, interior finishes, and the sanctuary itself — the work that turns a finished building into a consecrated place.

The day we are building toward

The first Mass — and the first ordinations

From the seminary chapel to the cathedral: a seminarian prostrates himself where you helped lay the floor, and rises a priest. That day is the real groundbreaking’s real purpose.

Why we build

We are not building a building. We are forming priests.

Stone and glass are only the shell. Inside it, men will hear their vocation tested and confirmed at daily Mass, chant the Liturgy of the Hours morning and evening, sit in silence before the Blessed Sacrament — and one day lie prostrate on that floor at their ordination.

Every benefactor who funds a window or a wall has a part in every priest formed inside them, and in every parish those priests will serve for the rest of their lives.

“No one can outdo God in generosity.” Give, and watch what He builds with it — a chapel, yes, but first, priests after His own heart.
